title: Signed-payload strkey whose inner payload is 65 bytes, one more than the XDR maximum of 64
why: The XDR type is opaque payload<64>, so a 65-byte payload has no XDR form; a decoder that checks only the SEP layout (length prefix and padding) accepts it.

reject.note: The SEP layout holds, but XDR opaque payload<64> has no 65-byte form.

known_divergences.detail: Executed on 16.3.0, 16.3.1 and 16.4.1: the v16 StrKey decoder (unchanged since 16.0.0) checks the checksum but not the per-type payload rules and returns a payload. The strict decoder exists only on the v17 line, where 17.2.0 and later reject this vector.
known_divergences.evidence: probe vector 9S3 (evidence/sdk-matrix), executed on js 16.3.0, js 16.3.1 and js 16.4.1

notes: Built by xdrcheck-corpus synth from corpus/recipes/strkey/synthetic-gap-vectors.signed-payload-65-byte.json. The text was encoded from the stated payload with an independent SEP-0023 encoder (version byte, payload, CRC16-XModem little-endian, RFC 4648 base32 without padding) and decoded back by the same rules; no SDK output was used. Executed in every probe column as vector 9S3 (evidence/sdk-matrix/vectors/vectors.json).
